title: CrescentCare Assurance Journal — POC & Audit Evidence
summary: Working journal capturing the CrescentCare POC security questionnaire responses, evidence index, chain-of-custody notes from the on-site workshop, and recommended remediation/next steps for Private deployment (VPC + customer KMS). Contains mixed polish: formal evidence mapping followed by field notes from workshop day 1 and action items.
body:
Purpose:
This document is a living assurance journal for the CrescentCare private deployment POC. Goal is twofold: 1) provide an auditable index of artifacts we used to answer CrescentCare's infosec questionnaire and 2) capture workshop/triage notes from the 2025-01-28 on-site security review so the audit team has context for any follow-ups.

Top-level summary:
- Deployment mode: Redwood Private (customer VPC, customer-managed KMS).
- Primary controls exercised: network isolation (VPC + private subnets), IAM + role separation, customer KMS for model key wrapping, ephemeral compute nodes, and enhanced logging to Splunk (customer tenant).
- Risk posture: low for data-in-flight/in-rest with current config; outstanding items: org-level SMPC/HSM integration proof, formal KMS rotation policy artifacts, and automated evidence extraction for future audit runs.

Evidence index (mapped to artifact filenames and short description):
- cc_network_design_v1.pdf — Network architecture diagram showing VPC peering, transit gateway, and service endpoints (redacted customer CIDRs).
- cc_kms_integration_snippet.txt — Terraform snippet demonstrating customer KMS keyalias used for envelope encryption (sensitive values redacted).
- cc_hsm_control_matrix.csv — Control mapping for HSM provider (vendor supplied) and required audit logs.
- cc_audit_trail_sample.log — Sample event log from a private node showing model load, client auth, and KMS wrap calls (timestamps included).
- cc_access_matrix.xlsx — Matrix of least-privilege roles and who currently holds them in the POC account.
- cc_workshop_minutes_2025-01-28.docx — Meeting notes and decision log from on-site (this doc contains the unstructured notes).
- cc_chain_of_custody.txt — Short notes on artifact provenance and who last touched evidence files.
- cc_pen_test_summary.pdf — High-level results summary from vendor quick-scan (non-exhaustive) performed during the POC window.

Questionnaire responses (authoritative answers we submitted to CrescentCare):
- Q: Where are encryption keys stored? A: Customer-managed KMS in their cloud account; Redwood Private is configured to reference the KMS via a restricted IAM role; no keys stored in Redwood-managed control plane. See cc_kms_integration_snippet.txt.
- Q: Do you have HSM-backed signing? A: We support customer-provided HSMs for key material. For this POC we confirmed vendor HSM integration was available (see cc_hsm_control_matrix.csv). Final attestation pending live audit.
- Q: How are logs protected? A: Application and audit logs are forwarded over a dedicated private endpoint to customer Splunk tenant with TLS and mutual auth. Logs are stored in S3-like bucket with SSE-KMS (customer key) and object lifecycle policies.

Field notes from 2025-01-28 on-site workshop (raw / unedited):
- 09:15 intro with CrescentCare SecOps (Maya). Clarified scope: PII never stored by Redwood; models access ephemeral cache only; persistent artifacts are only logs and metrics forwarded to customer systems.
- 10:00 walked through network diagram. Action: add explicit egress-deny for all subnets except required service endpoints. Owner: Ravi (due 2025-02-05).
- 11:10 demonstration of key wrap. Observed: KMS requests appear from Redwood's ephemeral compute role; CrescentCare asked for increased granularity on requester principal. Action: produce IAM policy dump and principal ARN list. Owner: Asha (due 2025-01-31).
- 14:30 log sampling exercise. Found one log entry with masked user id but not hashed. Action: redact routine to be added to pipeline for PII. Owner: Liam (due 2025-02-10).

Chain-of-custody and artifact provenance:
- All artifacts generated by Redwood engineering staff in the POC account were copied to the secure evidence bucket (customer-visible) and a checksum was recorded. The cc_chain_of_custody.txt file contains per-file sha256 and owner initials (AM, LO, RP). Any changes to artifacts post-upload are recorded as new files with timestamps.

Outstanding audit gaps and recommended mitigations (prioritized):
1) HSM attestation: Customer requested vendor-signed attestation for HSM firmware and key ceremony. Recommendation: coordinate vendor attestation package and schedule an HSM audit (owner: Morgan; target 2025-02-28).
2) KMS rotation policy: Need written rotation schedule and automated rotation proof. Recommendation: add scheduled rotation job and an evidence export demonstrating a rotation event (owner: Asha; target 2025-02-14).
3) Automated evidence export: CrescentCare asked for a one-click ZIP of all artifacts for audit. Recommendation: add an artifacts-export lambda in POC account, triggered by a Jira approval (owner: Ravi; target 2025-03-01).

Remediation work items (short checklist):
- [ ] Produce IAM principal list and attach to questionnaire answer (Asha).
- [ ] Implement subnet egress-deny and document exception list (Ravi).
- [ ] Add PII redaction hook to logging pipeline; deploy to private POC cluster (Liam).
- [ ] Collect vendor HSM attestation and place in evidence bucket (Morgan).
- [ ] Create artifacts-export job and link to Confluence runbook (Ravi/Asha).

Notes on verification and reproducibility:
- Repro steps for log sample: within POC account run: 
  ./scripts/collect-log-sample --start 2025-01-27T00:00Z --end 2025-01-29T00:00Z --filter "model_load,auth" > cc_audit_trail_sample.log
- Repro steps for KMS binding snippet: see cc_kms_integration_snippet.txt. DO NOT share private keys; public snippets only.

Compliance readiness status (quick rubric):
- Encryption at rest: Compliant (customer KMS in place).
- Encryption in transit: Compliant (mTLS for control plane + TLS for data plane).
- Access controls: Mostly compliant (need refined principals list & service account minimization).
- Logging & monitoring: Mostly compliant (need PII redaction automation and longer retention proofs).
- Change management: Partial (evidence of code changes exists, need documented deployment approvals).

Appendix: Useful references and links (internal):
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/CrescentCare+Private+Deployment+Runbook
- Terraform module PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-private-deployments/pull/214
- Jira epic: JIRA-SEC-842 (CrescentCare POC security follow-ups)

Working log (chronological snippets):
- 2025-01-16: kickoff call — confirmed scope and initial evidence list.
- 2025-01-20: collected initial logs, shared sample with CrescentCare SecOps.
- 2025-01-28: on-site workshop (minutes in cc_workshop_minutes_2025-01-28.docx).
- 2025-01-30: delivered preliminary questionnaire answers and evidence index.

Contact points: Asha Mehta (solutions-eng, lead) — asha@redwood.ai; Ravi Patel (platform-eng) — rpatel@redwood.ai; CrescentCare SecOps lead: Maya Thompson — maya@crescentcare.org

This file is intentionally a mixture of polished artifacts (evidence index, questionnaire text) and raw field notes so auditors can see the context behind decisions. For any artifact that will be shared externally, ensure sensitive fields are redacted and that a checksum is published in cc_chain_of_custody.txt.
evidence_items: cc_audit_trail_sample.log — sample audit log extracted from POC nodes
